title: Food Service Managers
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of an organization or department that serves food and beverages.

tasks.text: Monitor budgets and payroll records, and review financial transactions to ensure that expenditures are authorized and budgeted.
Coordinate assignments of cooking personnel to ensure economical use of food and timely preparation.
Arrange for equipment maintenance and repairs, and coordinate a variety of services, such as waste removal and pest control.
Plan menus and food utilization, based on anticipated number of guests, nutritional value, palatability, popularity, and costs.
Monitor employee and patron activities to ensure liquor regulations are obeyed.
Monitor food preparation methods, portion sizes, and garnishing and presentation of food to ensure that food is prepared and presented in an acceptable manner.
Monitor compliance with health and fire regulations regarding food preparation and serving, and building maintenance in lodging and dining facilities.
Keep records required by government agencies regarding sanitation or food subsidies.
Maintain food and equipment inventories, and keep inventory records.
Record the number, type, and cost of items sold to determine which items may be unpopular or less profitable.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Schedule and receive food and beverage deliveries, checking delivery contents to verify product quality and quantity.
Organize and direct worker training programs, resolve personnel problems, hire new staff, and evaluate employee performance in dining and lodging facilities.
Test cooked food by tasting and smelling it to ensure palatability and flavor conformity.
Count money and make bank deposits.
Order and purchase equipment and supplies.
Assess staffing needs and recruit staff, using methods such as newspaper advertisements or attendance at job fairs.
Estimate food, liquor, wine, and other beverage consumption to anticipate amounts to be purchased or requisitioned.
Review work procedures and operational problems to determine ways to improve service, performance, or safety.
Review menus and analyze recipes to determine labor and overhead costs, and assign prices to menu items.
Greet guests, escort them to their seats, and present them with menus and wine lists.
Establish standards for personnel performance and customer service.
Schedule staff hours and assign duties.
Investigate and resolve complaints regarding food quality, service, or accommodations.
Perform some food preparation or service tasks, such as cooking, clearing tables, and serving food and drinks when necessary.
Take dining reservations.
Create specialty dishes and develop recipes to be used in dining facilities.
Schedule use of facilities or catering services for events such as banquets or receptions, and negotiate details of arrangements with clients.
Establish and enforce nutritional standards for dining establishments, based on accepted industry standards.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: Food Services Solutions DayCap, Intuit QuickBooks.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Microsoft Project, ReServe Interactive.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
